en: The Sūtra of the Questions of the Upāsikā Vimalā, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Gautama Prajñāruci of Central India during the Northern Wei Dynasty.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Bhagavat was staying in the City of Śrāvastī at the Palace of Tranquility.
In the palace’s multi-storied lecture hall, at that time, the laywoman Vimalā, the laywoman Bhadrā, and other such laywomen went to where the Buddha was.
Having arrived at the Buddha’s location, they prostrated with their heads at his feet; having paid homage at the Buddha’s feet, they withdrew and sat to one side.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the laywoman Vimalā, saying:
"O laywoman! Are you not practicing heedfulness? Is your mind not indolent?"
The upāsikā said,
“I am neither indolent nor do I practice with negligence.
The Buddha addressed the upāsikā Vimalā, saying:
“How is it that you are always free from indolence?
Furthermore, how do you practice without negligence?
The laywoman Vimalā replied to the Buddha:
“World-Honored One!

I always rise early to sweep the ground of the Buddha’s stupa. Having swept it, I plaster and repair the four sides and four areas; once they are purified and plastered, I scatter flowers and burn incense. After making such offerings, I then enter my room.”

Having entered the dwelling, he next enters into meditative concentration (*dhyāna*), cultivates the four sublime abodes (*brahmavihāra*), does not depart from the three refuges, and upholds the five precepts, always and constantly acting in this manner.
"I am not indolent; I practice without negligence.
Having spoken these words, the laywoman Vimalā addressed the Buddha again:
"World-Honored One!"
I do not yet know what kind of meritorious reward will be obtained from the roots of goodness gained by sweeping the ground of the Buddha’s stūpa,
nor what kind of meritorious reward will be obtained from the roots of goodness gained by plastering and adorning its four sides?
What is the karmic reward obtained from the roots of goodness gained by scattering flowers and burning incense as offerings to the Buddha’s stūpas?
What is the karmic reward obtained from the roots of goodness gained through the four dhyānas, the four brahma-vihāras, the three refuges, and the five precepts?
“I only pray that the World-Honored One will explain this for me.
The Buddha told the laywoman Vimalā:
“Sweeping the ground of a Buddhist stupa yields five kinds of meritorious retribution.”
What are the five?
First, one’s own mind is pure, such that others, upon seeing it, give rise to a pure mind;
second, one is beloved by others.
Third, the hearts of devas rejoice;
fourth, they accumulate karma of upright conduct;
fifth, at the end of their lives, they are reborn in the heavens of the good realms.
"Vimala, you should know that such is the karmic reward for sweeping the ground of a Buddha-stūpa.

Vimala, you should know that if a person has faith in the Buddha, fashions a circular mandala shape upon the ground of a Buddha-stūpa, scatters flowers, burns incense, and makes offerings in this manner, I declare that when that person’s body breaks up at the end of life, they will be reborn in Pūrvavideha, where they will possess wealth, joy, and sovereignty;
and when their life there ends, they will be reborn in the Nirmāṇarati Heaven."

"Vimala, you should know that if a person has faith in the Buddha and performs offerings by drawing a crescent shape on the ground of a stūpa, scattering flowers, and burning incense—having made such offerings, I say that when that person’s body breaks up at the end of life, they will be reborn in Godānīya, where they will possess wealth, joy, and sovereignty;
and when their life there ends, they will be reborn in Tuṣita Heaven."

“Vimala, you should know that if a person has faith in the Buddha and, at a stūpa of the Buddha, smears the ground in the four directions, scatters flowers, and burns incense—performing such offerings—I say that when that person’s body breaks up and their life ends, they will be reborn in Uttarakuru, wealthy, joyful, and sovereign;
and when their life there ends, they will be reborn in the Yāma Heaven.”

“Vimala, you should know that if a person has faith in the Buddha, fashions the form of a human face, smears the ground of a stūpa, scatters flowers, and burns incense—making such offerings as these—I say that when that person’s body breaks up and their life ends, they will be reborn in Jambudvīpa, wealthy, joyful, and sovereign;
and at the end of their lifespan, they will be reborn in the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven.”
“Vimala, you should know that such is the fruit and retribution for all roots of goodness derived from anointing the ground of a stūpa, scattering flowers, and burning incense.

Vimala, you should know that if a person enters dhyāna and cultivates the four brahma-vihāras, takes refuge in the Buddha, Dharma, and Saṅgha, and upholds the five precepts, I say that this person’s roots of goodness are immeasurable and innumerable, their meritorious retribution is inexhaustible and endless, and they shall later attain nirvāṇa.”
"Vimala, you should know that if a person takes refuge in the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas and cultivates the collection of precepts, they will not be able to attain such inexhaustible nirvāṇa."

Why is this? Because the karmic retribution obtained from upholding the five precepts and practicing the four Brahma-vihāras through meditation cannot be received anywhere other than in nirvāṇa, owing to the great abundance of such merit.
When the Blessed One had spoken thus, the laywoman Vimalā conceived a doubt in her mind and remained silent.

At that time, the Blessed One, knowing her thoughts, extended his broad and long tongue from his mouth; it completely covered his own face, both ears, both eyes, as well as both nostrils, and then pervaded the entire expanse of space. Having covered the space, he withdrew it back into his mouth. Once it was withdrawn, he spoke again to the laywoman Vimalā:
"Have you ever seen anyone who speaks falsely, who uses double-tongued speech, harsh words, or frivolous chatter, possessing such a physical mark of a tongue as this?"
At that time, having heard these words, the laywoman Vimalā rose from her seat, joined her palms toward the Buddha, and said to him:
“World-Honored One!
"I have never seen such a thing.
Even among those who speak the truth, there has never been a tongue like this, much less among those who speak falsehoods.
Only the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, having always spoken the truth since beginningless time, has attained such a tongue."
At that time, the laywoman Vimalā, knowing that the Buddha spoke the truth, was freed from doubt and filled with joy; she praised him in verse, saying:
"In thousands of billions of kalpas, I have never before recalled seeing such a supreme jewel of Dharma, nor do I recall having made offerings to it."
"Today I have been able to see, Such a lamp of the world;
having seen him thus, I have been able to hear the supreme Dharma.
At that time, the World-Honored One replied to the laywoman Vimalā in verse:
“Having heard this, you have already become noble; this is the truly supreme treasure of the Dharma, the pure and tranquil teaching by which one enters the city of Nirvāṇa.

When the World-Honored One had finished speaking, the laywoman Vimalā was filled with great joy. The assembly of bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās, as well as all the devas, humans, asuras, gandharvas, and others, having heard what the Buddha said, praised him, saying:
“Excellent! This sutra is the cause for humans and devas, And it is also the path to nirvāṇa.
The practitioner proceeds toward the realm of humans and devas, And likewise advances through the gateway to nirvāṇa.”
The merit of translating this sutra is universally bestowed upon all sentient beings;
may they swiftly cultivate the path of causes and attain the realms of humans, devas, and nirvana.
The Sūtra of the Inquiry of the Upāsikā Vimalā (Vimalā-upāsikā-paripṛcchā-sūtra)
